o: Nothing; wait for the CA decision
Move for new trial at the CA before its judgment becomes final
File a new case
Go straight to the SC
qs.ex: Rule 124, Sec. 14.

qs.tw: The case reaches the SC en banc. The Justices are equally divided on acquittal, and re-deliberation does not break the tie.
o: The conviction is affirmed
The conviction is reversed and Cris is acquitted
The case is remanded
The Chief Justice decides
qs.ex: Rule 125, Sec. 3.

S.title: Getting and serving a search warrant
S.base: Police want a search warrant for Dina's house in Pasig for illegal firearms. No criminal case has been filed.

o: Any court in the Philippines
Any court within whose territorial jurisdiction the crime was committed; or, for compelling reasons stated, any court in the judicial region
Only the Supreme Court
Only the court of the police station's location
qs.ex: Rule 126, Sec. 2.

qs.tw: A criminal case for the same offense is already pending in a Pasig RTC branch.
o: Any Pasig court
Only the court where the criminal case is pending
Any court in the region
The executive judge
qs.ex: Rule 126, Sec. 2 (last paragraph).

qs.tw: The judge issues the warrant after reading only the applicant's affidavit, without asking any questions.
o: Yes, the affidavit is under oath
No. The judge must personally examine the applicant and witnesses through searching questions and answers, in writing and under oath
Yes, if the affidavit is detailed
Only if the prosecutor signed
qs.ex: Rule 126, Secs. 4–5.

qs.tw: The warrant says nothing about the time of service. Police search at 11 p.m.
o: Yes, any time is fine
No. A warrant must be served in the daytime unless the affidavit says the property is on the person or in the place, and the warrant allows service at any time
Yes, if the occupant is awake
Only on weekends
qs.ex: Rule 126, Sec. 9.

qs.tw: Police seize the guns. Dina is present, but they leave no receipt.
qs.q: What did they fail to do?
o: Nothing
Give the lawful occupant a detailed receipt for the property seized
Call the media
Photograph the house
qs.ex: Rule 126, Sec. 11.

qs.tw: Police bring the seized items to their headquarters and keep them there.
o: Yes, police hold evidence
No. They must deliver the property to the issuing judge, with a true inventory verified under oath
Yes, for 30 days
Only if no case is filed
qs.ex: Rule 126, Sec. 12(a).

qs.tw: While validly searching for guns, officers see a bag of shabu lying openly on a table.
o: No, the warrant covers only firearms
Yes, under plain view: they were lawfully there, came upon it inadvertently, and its illegal character was immediately apparent
Only with a second warrant
Only if Dina consents
qs.ex: Plain view doctrine.

qs.tw: Instead, they pry open a locked drawer, find personal letters unrelated to firearms, and seize them.
o: Yes, they were found during a valid search
No. They are outside the warrant and not in plain view
Yes, if they are relevant
Only on the civil aspect
qs.ex: The warrant limits what may be seized; plain view requires the item to be visible without further search.

qs.tw: Dina wants to quash the warrant. No criminal case has been filed yet.
qs.q: Where does she file the motion?
o: Any court
The court that issued the warrant
The DOJ
The Court of Appeals
qs.ex: Rule 126, Sec. 14. Once a criminal case is filed, the motion goes to the court where it is filed.

b: Downgrading the charge or dropping an accused
Motion + notice to offended party + leave of court
Formal only, with leave, no prejudice
Accused waives the right to present evidence

a: To settle, or for his convenience
b: For insufficiency of evidence or denial of speedy trial
Acts as acquittal; cannot be refiled

a: Offense not punishable by RP, life, or death
b: Offense punishable by RP, life, or death
Denied if evidence of guilt is strong; hearing required

F.t: Bail after RTC conviction — which court?
a: Trial court may act, even after notice of appeal
b: Judgment changed the offense from non-bailable to bailable
No expiry; officer reports within 10 days

a: Dismissed; civil action may go against the estate
b: Criminal and civil ex delicto extinguished; independent civil action survives

a: Searching inquiry + prosecution must present evidence
Grounds c, d, e, f, h

b: Extinction of liability or double jeopardy

F.t: Separate civil action pending criminal case
Effect of acquittal on civil liability
a: Civil liability may still be awarded
b: Court finds the act did not exist or accused did not do it

a: Ask for PI with waiver of Art. 125; finish in 15 days
b: Ask within 5 days from learning of the filing

a: Affected evidence set aside and retaken
b: Old evidence stands; new evidence added

a: Prosecution witness (sick, or leaving the country)
Before the court where the case is pending, with the accused present or notified
b: Defense witness (sick, far away with no means, etc.)
Before a judge, a member of the bar, or an inferior court judge

a: Notice of appeal to the CA
b: Petition for review (Rule 42) to the CA

a: Offended spouse only; must include both parties
Attachment available in the criminal case
b: Civil action reserved or filed separately
Seek attachment in the civil case

N: Investigating officer dismisses or issues subpoena
Judge evaluates the resolution for warrant
Additional evidence on judge's order / resolve probable cause
PI after waiving Art. 125 must end
Ask for PI after learning the case was filed without one
Execute warrant of arrest; report within 10 days after
Penalty above which bail pending appeal may be denied for a listed circumstance
Destierro: release after this much preventive imprisonment
Bondsmen produce the accused after forfeiture
Arraignment from court acquiring jurisdiction over the accused
Detained accused: raffle and transmit records
Maximum suspension of arraignment for petition for review
Provisional dismissal becomes permanent (penalty ≤ 6 years or fine)
Pre-trial from court acquiring jurisdiction over the accused
Time to prepare for trial after not-guilty plea
Trial starts from receipt of pre-trial order
New trial after an order for new trial must start
Defense witness distance ground for conditional examination
Motion for leave to file demurrer, after prosecution rests
File demurrer after notice of leave
Surrender and move for leave after promulgation in absentia
Appeal from promulgation or notice of final order
New appeal period after denial of MR/MNT
Clerk transmits records after notice of appeal
Appellant's brief / appellee's brief / reply brief (CA)
Motion for reconsideration in the CA
Witnesses from the locality when occupant and family are absent
Requisites to discharge an accused as state witness
Non-waivable grounds to quash: a, b, g, i
